*****NOTE FROM THE CITY: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency
and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20
(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf).
Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of
September 28, 2021, at 2:00 P.M. for open session as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure
  distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
  comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
  number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
  received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of the public hearings, will be made part of the official public
  record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

  2. In Person: The Library Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) will be open to provide members
  of the public with an opportunity to address the Legislative Body on Open Session Items.

  3. Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
  >On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for
details.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities Act

Inglewood, California
  September 28, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  September 28, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint
  Powers Authority at the hour of 2:02 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Joint Powers
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Joint Powers Authority officials and
  personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, and Joint Powers
  Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired
  if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council/Successor
  Agency/Housing Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on the Agendas.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. DR-1, Adoption of a
  resolution establishing the City’s tax-supported appropriations limitation for Fiscal Year
  2021-2022, DR-2, Adoption of a resolution approving and adopting the Fiscal Year 2021-
  2022 Annual Budget, and DR-4, Adoption of a resolution accepting CARES Act CDBG-
  CV Round 3 funds.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Dotson, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  September 24, 2021, in the amount of $3,859,352.83 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PROCLAMATION – BREAST CANCER AWARENESS MONTH. Mayor Butts
  read a proclamation recognizing October as Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

  PRESENTATION – KATHY GIVENS. Senator Steven Bradford, 35th District,
  presented Kathy Givens with a Resolution honoring her for 37 years of service to the City
  of Inglewood.
   September 28, 2021

  ACCOMMODATION – KATHY GIVENS.  The City Council presented Kathy
  Givens with an Accommodation from the City of Inglewood for 37 years of service.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on June 15, 2021,
  June 22, 2021, June 29, 2021, June 29, 2021 (Special), and July 14, 2021 (Special), be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

125  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the City Attorney’s Office recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Silvia Aguirre for alleged personal injuries; sidewalk defect on July 9, 2021.
  2. Elizabeth Garcia for alleged personal injuries; sidewalk defect February 14, 2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A-1 and A-2. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-249 APPROVED – UNIVERSAL PROTECTION
  SERVICE, LP, DBA ALLIED UNIVERSAL PROTECTION SERVICES, LP;
  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – ALLIED UNIVERSAL PROTECTION SERVICES,
  LP; RESOLUTION NO. 21-150 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR
  2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated September 28, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of a two (2)-year Cooperative Purchase Agreement (with the
  option to extend up to two (2) additional years in one-year increments) with Universal
  Protection Service, LP, dba Allied Universal Protection Services, LP, for unarmed
  security officers at Inglewood City Hall, the Senior Center, City Yard, Main Library, and
  Crenshaw-Imperial Branch Library.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Cooperative Purchase Agreement No. 21-249
  in a total annual amount not to exceed $977,081.85 (includes a 20% contingency in the
  amount of $162,846.97); 2) Authorize payment of outstanding invoices submitted by
  Allied Universal Protection Services, LP, for unarmed security officer services provided
  for months of May 2021 through September 2021, in an amount not to exceed $228,750;
  and 3) Adopt Resolution No. 21-150 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET TO
  INCLUDE $705,832 IN ADDITIONAL FUNDS FOR UNARMED SECURITY
  GUARD SERVICES

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

142  AGREEMENT NO. 20-138 TERMINATED – SERVICON SYSTEMS, INC;
  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – INCURRED COSTS BY SERVICON SYSTEMS,
  INC; AGREEMENT NO. 21-250 APPROVED – UNIVERSAL BUILDING
  MAINTENANCE, LLC DBA ALLIED UNIVERSAL JANITORIAL SERVICES;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-151 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 ANNUAL BUDGET; STAFF DIRECTED TO RE-BID JANITORIAL
  MAINTENANCE SUPPLIES. Staff report dated September 28, 2021, was presented
  recommending termination of Agreement No. 20-138 with Servicon Systems, Inc.

  2
   September 28, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Terminate Agreement No. 20-138; 2) Authorize
  payment of costs incurred by Servicon Systems, Inc., in a total amount of $710,416
  (includes $533,875 for janitorial services provided from May 2020 through August 2021,
  and a contingency in the amount of $176,541 for September 2021); 3) Approve an
  emergency four (4)-month agreement with Universal Building Maintenance, LLC dba
  Allied Universal Janitorial Services to provide janitorial services in the amount of
  $599,268; 4) Adopt Resolution No. 21-151 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2020/2021 ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  INCREASE FUNDING TO PAY FOR JANITORIAL SERVICES

  and; 4) Direct staff to re-bid Janitorial Maintenance Services. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  AGREEMENT NO. 21-251 APPROVED – MOU FOR SUB-REGIONAL
  PARATRANSIT  SERVICES  WITH  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY
  METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY (LACMTA). Staff report
  dated September 28, 2021, was presented recommending approval of the attached
  Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for sub-regional Paratransit Services with Los
  Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA) for receipt of
  approximately $200,000 in Proposition A funding, annually, from July 1, 2021, through
  June 30, 2026.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-25, MOU for Sub-Regional
  Paratransit Services with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (LACMTA). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-252 APPROVED – L.A.
  BUSINESS PRINTING SERVICES. Staff report dated September 28, 2021, was
  presented recommending award of a contract and approval of an agreement with L.A.
  Business Printing Services, for the Community Information Guide Project, Graphic
  Design and Printing Services, per Request for Proposal No. RFP-0169.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-252 in an
  amount not to exceed $213,141.84. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 20-023 APPROVED – BEAR
  COMMUNICATIONS, INC. Staff report dated September 28, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Agreement No. 20-023 with Bear
  Communications, Inc., extending the agreement an additional year (with the option to
  extend an additional one (1) year) to continue providing preventive maintenance and on-
  call emergency repair services for the Police Department’s radio equipment.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve amendment to Agreement No. 20-023 in a total
  amount not to exceed $74,823.16 (includes contingency in the amount of $10,000). The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 21-253 APPROVED - MORBARK, LLC. Staff report dated

  3
   September 28, 2021

  September 28, 2021, was presented recommending approval of a cooperative purchase
  agreement with Morbark, LLC, for the purchase of two (2) Morbark brush chippers.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve cooperative purchase Agreement No. 21-253 in the
  amount of $115,913. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 21-254 APPROVED –
  CALIFORNIA RECYCLE TEAM, INC. DBA ELECTRONIC WASTE

  Response Litter Removal Program, per Bid No. RFB-0132 Reissue.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 21-254 in an

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

142  RESOLUTION NO. 21-152 ADOPTED – CITY’S TAX-SUPPORTED
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMITATION FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022, AS
  REQUIRED BY THE “GANN AMENDMENT” TO THE CALIFORNIA
  CONSTITUTION.  Staff report dated September 28, 2021, was presented
  recommending adoption of a resolution establishing the City’s tax-supported

  Keauonna Buckhanon, Budget Manager presented the Staff Report dated September 28,

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that Resolution

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD ESTABLISHING AN APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

101  RESOLUTION NO. 21-153 ADOPTED – APPROVING AND ADOPTING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report dated September 28,
  2021, was presented recommending adoption of a resolution approving and adopting the
  Fiscal Year 2021-2022 Annual Budget.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that Resolution No. 21-153 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

  4
   September 28, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

131.8  RESOLUTION NO. 21-155 ADOPTED – CARES ACT CDBG-CV ROUND 3
